title: 48 mornings, no gaps
headline: 48 mornings, no gaps. The prices are a day old.
dek: The board has published every morning since Sep 28: 48 commits in 48 days, none missing. 47 landed within a minute of the 08:15 Central schedule (median 7 seconds); the first, the launch, took more than nine hours. The prices were exactly one day old when they went up on every one of the 47 mornings measured: the page says it was updated today, and its prices are yesterday's. The sales behind the flags run older, a median of 3 days. Every move is unconfirmed.
why_now: A board that says every number carries its source and its date should say how current it is. After seven weeks of running on its own, the board has a record to read, and the honest summary is steady, on time, and a day behind the market by design.
risk: A publish that lands on time proves the job ran, not that every number is right: the checks for that are the language rule, the feed contract and a person reading the Files. A commit every day also means the data changed every day, since a publish with nothing new commits nothing. The first morning is the manual launch, so "on schedule" is measured on the 47 mornings after it. The sales figure comes from only 12 mornings, since sales began to be dated on Nov 3. A missed or failed publish would show in our private daily report the same day. No sale was checked behind any of the moves here. This is not a read on whether these prices are high or low.
what_to_watch: Whether the next 48 mornings are as steady, and whether the sales age comes down from its 2 to 5 days. Whether the prices stay exactly one day old; a morning with older ones would mean the nightly pull failed. And the label: the morning one of these cards has a checked sale, its row stops reading Unconfirmed.
source: The board repository's own commit history, Sep 28 to Nov 14, 2026 ("Board data" commits and each morning's meta.json); TCGplayer market prices via tcgcsv.com

foot: Market price: TCGplayer's average of recent completed sales of the same card, condition and printing (help.tcgplayer.com). The record: the board repository's commit history (git log), the 48 commits titled "Board data <date>" from 2026-09-28 to 2026-11-14, one for each of the 48 calendar days. Time: each commit's author time in Central time against 08:15; 47 landed 2 to 13 seconds after it (median 7); the first, on Sep 28, at 17:26 Central, was the launch. Price age: the day of each commit minus the tcgcsv as-of date in that morning's meta.json: exactly 1 day on all 47 mornings where it was dated (the launch morning had none). Sales age: the same against the sales as-of date, on the 12 mornings it was dated (Nov 3 to Nov 14): median 3 days, range 2 to 5. A row's own price date is the day TCGplayer's price last changed (tcgcsv stores a price only when it changes): on Nov 14's 7-day list, 7 of the 10 rows read Nov 13, one Nov 12 and two Nov 11. The table: four cards from that list, chosen to show those dates; start-of-week prices are worked back from the listed price and its rounded change, so within a dollar. The list: up to 10 Pokémon cards worth $20 or more that moved 5% or more in a week; with no checked sales, a move shows only if it's 60% or less, the lowest listing moved the same way by at least a quarter as much, the price changed in the last 2 days, and the card trades. Unconfirmed: no sale checked by Mission Control's Sale Integrity Layer in that window. Not advice.
